scope: Human aripiprazole striatal D2/3 PET occupancy only; not validation of neural activity, subjective effects, whole-brain dynamics, cognition, clinical response or safety.

sources.title: Kim et al. (2012), Predicting brain occupancy from plasma levels using PET, Table 1 and Results
sources.population: Healthy male volunteers, mean age 22.9 years
sources.design: Single oral administration; PET at baseline and 3, 45 and 120 hours; serial plasma measurements through 120 hours
sources.role: Published model calibration; these fitted parameter values are not held-out observations

sources.title: Ito et al. (2012), Effects of aripiprazole on dopamine synthesis in human brain, Table 1 and Results
sources.design: Single oral administration; 60-minute PET started 3.5 hours later; plasma concentration is the mean of samples at scan start and end
sources.role: Independent study observations; aggregate conditional comparison, not a prospectively blinded validation trial
sources.license: CC BY, original article attributed to Ito et al.

calibrationModels.maximumEvidence: Fixed 100% maximum in the published model, not a fitted measurement
calibrationModels.concentrationBasis: Total-plasma-equivalent effect compartment; not free brain concentration
calibrationModels.equations: dCe/dt = ke0(Cp - Ce); occupancy = Ce / (EC50 + Ce); ng/mL = nM × molecularWeight / 1000
calibrationModels.context: N=18 healthy men after a single oral administration. EC50 and ke0 were estimated together using serial human PET and plasma data. The NeuroScope plasma compartment and virtual bolus are different from the published oral PK model.
limits: PET measures D2/3 radioligand displacement, whereas the app represents a combined D2 target. This is a striatal calibration, not an extrastriatal or whole-brain occupancy measurement.
The effect compartment is an empirical delay model. It does not identify blood–brain barrier permeability, a binding on/off rate, Kp,uu or a measured brain concentration.
The simulation transfers the published effect model to its simplified virtual plasma kinetics; route, absorption, patient variability and active metabolites are not reconstructed.
Competition with other compounds, altered endogenous drive, repeated exposure and links to functional neural responses are unvalidated transfers.
Parameter confidence intervals do not describe patient prediction intervals. Occupancy does not specify receptor activation or clinical response.

benchmarks.inputBasis: Reported total plasma mean; equilibrium approximation Ce = Cp for a conditional concentration comparison. No concentration history is invented.
benchmarks.oldModelBasis: NeuroScope 3.2 equilibrium Ki occupancy: Ki=0.34 nM, freeFraction=0.01, Kp,uu=1 and endogenous D2 drive=2/3. These are frozen for the before/after comparison.
benchmarks.evaluation: Unweighted mean absolute error in percentage points across four published regional group means. Regions share participants; the four errors are not independent observations. Two additional n=2 range comparisons are shown separately and excluded from MAE.
limitations: The observations were not used to choose or fit EC50 or ke0. They were inspected during development, so this is an external-data comparison, not a blinded or prospective holdout.

Observed plasma means are inputs, not predictions. Acute scans may precede effect-site equilibrium; unavailable individual concentration histories prevent testing the dynamic delay against this study.
Applying a nonlinear curve to a group mean does not equal averaging individual predictions. SD is participant variability, not a confidence interval or an acceptance threshold.
The original study measured caudate and putamen separately; the app uses one striatal curve. Remaining regional residuals are reported without retuning to these observations.

The measured active metabolite was small but nonzero; parent-only modeling does not explicitly represent it. No clinical, cognitive, electrophysiological or whole-brain validation follows from this comparison.
